entry.label: Transduction
entry.description: Transduction explains why a citizen's life becomes a case, a need becomes a code, work becomes a metric and strategy becomes a local instruction. The message is changed by the receiving world's categories and capacities.
entry.canonical_definition: A boundary process that transforms signals, meanings or varieties from one domain into a form another domain can register and act upon; it is never assumed to be lossless.

profile.title: Transduction
profile.canonical_definition: A boundary process that transforms signals, meanings or varieties from one domain into a form another domain can register and act upon; it is never assumed to be lossless.
profile.summary: Transduction explains why a citizen's life becomes a case, a need becomes a code, work becomes a metric and strategy becomes a local instruction. The message is changed by the receiving world's categories and capacities. Beer distinguishes a channel's capacity from the transducer's capacity at a boundary. His third principle requires the latter to match at least the former.
profile.why_it_matters: Transformation often fails at boundaries rather than within units. Seeing transduction reveals where meaning is lost, invented, protected or made actionable. Translation can discard a distinction that the communication channel could carry.
practice_connections: compare the sending and receiving codes
ask what is lost and newly created
design two-way transduction rather than one-way reporting
Compare the distinctions arriving at a boundary with those available after translation.
common_misreadings: the same information exists on both sides
A wider communication channel repairs every translation failure.
open_checks: Specify the relevant variety before applying this organisational principle elsewhere.
profile.editorial_note: Primary passages checked for this bounded research pass. Exposition and editorial comparisons remain distinct; named editorial acceptance is not implied by publication.
